rationales.1: The colored count strip (3 open, 2 caution, 2 closed, 2 no report) and the closure alert both sit in the first mobile viewport, so the go or no-go answer needs nothing but a glance and a scroll for the trail names.
rationales.2: Every status pairs a text label with a colored edge bar, and each of the four statuses keeps one hue and one rendering from the summary strip through every section.
rationales.3: Unreported trails get their own UNKNOWN section with the line that unknown is not the same as fine, the July 22 gap is an explicit italic row, snowpack carries a visible ESTIMATED badge with the sensor story, and every trail shows its own report time.
rationales.4: GO, GO WITH CARE, DO NOT GO, UNKNOWN is exactly the hiker's decision order in plain imperative language, with weather history and snowpack correctly demoted below the decision content.
rationales.5: Spacing rhythm, aligned label column, restrained palette and roughly three type sizes are held with discipline; only a faint stray rule artifact above the footer keeps this from the top band.
rationales.6: Long names, the burn cluster, and both unreported rows sit naturally in the row layout, and the dark mode is fully designed rather than inverted.
rationales.7: The signature reads as a board that reports only what it knows, and the honesty copy, the gap row, and the unknown section all reinforce it in a way that is true of a conditions service.
rationales.8: Mechanics are entirely conventional; the single deliberate break is the imperative section naming, which lives in the brand layer.
rationales.9: Lines like unknown is not the same as fine, and showing the gap as the gap it is, are calm, factual, and could not be published unchanged by a competitor.
rationales.10: The count strip rewards the habitual daily glance instantly, and nothing playful or mandatory stands between a returning user and the answer.
